answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: The reply orders the work as 'Fix first: these break reservations' (items 1 to 5, before launch), then 'Fix next', 'Smaller issues' and a 'Suggested order'. Under 'What I inferred' it says it 'didn't run VoiceOver or TalkBack', so the screen-reader points come from the markup, and leaves 'one pass on a real iPhone with VoiceOver and larger text turned on' to a person.

mapping.title: Basket hold expires after 10 minutes with no warning and no way back
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R1, B R1). Nothing on the site says the hold lasts ten minutes, and once it lapses Continue shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which says neither what happened nor what to do. That is D10's untimed hold and misleading error; 'Trying again fails every time, because the timer is never reset' is the same unhandled lapse.

mapping.title: Pick-up day and pick-up session are chosen separately and can disagree
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R2, B R2). The day chosen on the tool page and the session chosen in the basket are never checked against each other (the basket 'doesn't check it against that day'), and the run ends with the drill listed as 'pick up Saturday 17 October' against the 'Wednesday 21 October' session, so 'The desk can't tell which one is right'. That is D15, down to its own example.

mapping.title: Calendar accepts closed days; refused only on the confirm page with no link back
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R3, B R3). 'Every date can be chosen, including days the library is closed', and the refusal ('The library is closed on Friday 16 October… Choose another day') comes only on the confirm page, with 'no link to the place where you change it'. That is D06.

mapping.title: Days and sessions before the tool's available-from date are accepted
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R4, B R4). The calendar allows 'days before the tool is back' and the basket accepted the 10 Oct session for a pressure washer available from 17 Oct; offering only sessions on or after each tool's 'available from' date fixes D14.

mapping.title: Tapping Confirm twice books the tool twice
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R5, B R5). The Confirm button 'gives no visible sign that it's working for 1.5 s, and it isn't disabled', and tapping it twice gave FT-4471 and FT-4472 for the same drill. That is D12.

mapping.title: Basket not emptied after a confirmed booking
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R6, B R6). 'The basket also isn't emptied after a confirmed booking': the header still showed 'Basket (1)' on the confirmation (done) page. That is D18.

mapping.title: Truncated tool names make the two drills look the same on a phone
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R7, B R7). Names are cut to one line with an ellipsis, so at 375 px both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' and the battery difference the journey depends on is hidden. That is D03.

mapping.title: A search with no results silently keeps the old list
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R8, B R8). Searching 'hammer' still shows all 10 tools and 'Screen readers get no announcement', so members cannot tell that nothing matched. That is D02's no-match search with an empty status region.

mapping.title: Dark-mode 'Available from' badge fails text contrast
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R9, B R9). In dark mode the badge is #2f7d4a on #1d2622, 'a contrast of 3.07:1', for bold 16 px text that needs 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3). That is D04.

mapping.title: Faint calendar day borders and selected-day fill in dark mode
mapping.reason: Settled for B (A real-unseeded, B not-a-problem; see settled). The review gives this as one of 'two smaller dark-mode points', with no criterion and no fix, and says the selection still shows: 'The selected day is mostly shown by its 2 px border'. It does not show that a member cannot tell which day is chosen, and the faint borders surround day buttons their numbers already identify, so no harm to members is shown.

mapping.title: Loan-length dropdown shadow does not show in dark mode
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R11, B R11). A shadow is decoration; the review gives no measurement and does not say the open list blends into the page or that any option is hard to read.

mapping.title: On phones search and filters sit below all ten tools behind an icon-only button
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R12, B R12). Below 480 px the stylesheet moves the search form under the results ('about 2,100 px down the page'), 'The filters button is an icon with no visible word', and members 'don't know where the date filter is'. That is D01. The review places the keyboard/visual order mismatch on desktop rather than on phones, but it comes from the same order rules, and dropping them fixes D01.

mapping.title: Basket pick-up sessions shown in reverse order
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R13, B R13). row-reverse with wrap-reverse shows Wed 28 Oct at the top and Sat 10 Oct at the bottom on a phone, while 'Screen readers and the keyboard go through them in date order'. That is D11.

mapping.title: Confirm page rejects ordinary membership-number and mobile formats
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R14, B R14). 'ft-01234', 'FT 01234', 'FT01234', '+44 7700 900123' and '07700 900 123' are all rejected, with no normalising. That is D17.

mapping.title: Loan-length dropdown traps the keyboard and cannot be dismissed
mapping.reason: Settled as one item, as A had it (B split off the outside tap as its R16; see settled). While the list is open 'Tab cycles through the options instead of leaving the control' and 'Escape doesn't close it': D09's keyboard trap. 'Tapping outside doesn't close it either' is the same failure of the open list to let go, on the same control and with the same fix ('replace it with a native <select>'), so fixing what the item describes fixes D09.

mapping.title: Fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar covers the footer and desk phone number
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R16, B R17). Nothing pads the page clear of the fixed bar, so the footer with the desk phone number sits under the 'Reserve this tool' bar 'even when scrolled to the bottom'. That is D08's phone symptom; the review does not mention covered focused day buttons, so it reports the narrower part of the same defect.

mapping.title: 'Added to your basket' vanishes after 1.2 s with no next step nearby
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R17, B R18). 'The message disappears after 1.2 s' and the only way on is the 'Basket (1)' link at the top of the page: brief feedback with nothing lasting nearby. The item does not say members believe the tool is reserved, so under the D07/D26 rule it is D07, not D26.

mapping.title: Tool grid scrolls sideways at 320 px
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R18, B R19). minmax(330px, 1fr) gives '346 px of content in 320 px', so the page scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10). That is D05.

mapping.title: Confirm page 'Change' link drops the chosen session
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R19, B R20). The 'Change' link 'goes to the basket without the current session ticked'. That is D13.

mapping.title: Returning to the confirm page clears the details already typed
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R20, B R21). 'Coming back to confirm also clears the details the member already typed', so the member types them again on a phone. That is D22.

mapping.title: Three-tools-per-member limit not enforced in the basket
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R21, B R22). 'The three-tools-per-member rule isn't enforced in the basket.' That is D21.

mapping.title: Done page reads the tool name twice to screen readers
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R22, B R23). The hidden #c-tool copy makes screen readers read the tool name twice. The review uses 'confirmation page' for the done page throughout (it is also where it saw 'Basket (1)' after confirming), so this is D24.

mapping.title: 'Choose a pick-up session' error link points at a container that cannot take focus
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R23, B R24). Following the error link does not put keyboard or screen-reader members on the session radio buttons, so they have to hunt for the choices the error is about, and many members meet this error because the basket starts with no session selected. Not in the ground truth: D19 is the tool page's day message and D23 is the date being asked for twice.

mapping.title: No 'Skip to content' link on any page
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R24, B R25). The review shows no long repeated block that members must get past (the header it mentions holds the 'Basket (1)' link) and does not say headings or landmarks are missing, so on these short, phone-first pages it is a checklist remark with no harm shown.

settled.reason: Mapping decision: B's value. A's R10 and B's R10 are the same remark, the first of the 'two smaller dark-mode points' in review item 6. The review adds it 'While you're there', with no criterion and no fix, unlike the badge in the same item, which it says 'fails WCAG 1.4.3'. Its own words say the selection still shows ('The selected day is mostly shown by its 2 px border'), and it does not say the chosen day is hard to make out. The faint borders surround day buttons their numbers already identify, and WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 only for what is needed to identify a control or its state, so A's reading that both values fail 1.4.11 and leave a weak cue for the selected day goes beyond what the review shows. Like the shadow remark beside it (R11, not-a-problem in both files), it is a styling note with no harm to members shown.

settled.a: R15 = tool-library-D09, one item for Tab cycling, Escape and tapping outside
settled.b: R15 = tool-library-D09 (Tab cycling, Escape) and R16 = real-unseeded ('Tapping outside doesn't close it either')
settled.final: R15 = tool-library-D09, one item; B's R16 folded in
settled.reason: Alignment decision (A merged, B split): one item, as A had it. The review raises a single problem here: one numbered item about one control ('The loan-length dropdown misbehaves with a keyboard'), one fix ('replace it with a native <select>'), and it gives the outside tap as one more instance of the same failure, in the same breath: 'Escape doesn't close it. Tapping outside doesn't close it either.' B's own harm for its R16 (a member 'has to pick a loan length to close it') is D09's harm (the list cannot be left 'except by choosing an option') reached by touch instead of keys, so it is the same problem on the same control with the same cause and fix, not a distinct one. This matches how both graders treated review item 7, where the desktop keyboard-order point (another input, same cause and fix) stays inside the one D01 item; they split the review's sub-points only where it names a different element or failure (the three dark-mode points, 'The basket also isn't emptied', 'also clears the details'). B's ground for splitting, that 'D09 covers only the keyboard', is about the ground truth's scope rather than the review's problems; a broader statement maps to a defect when fixing what it describes fixes the defect, and a native select fixes D09's trap. B's R17 to R25 therefore pair with A's R16 to R24 (entries below).

Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are review item 11, the fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar covering the footer and the desk phone number. B's number is one higher because it split the loan-length dropdown into its R15 and R16.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are review item 12, 'Added to your basket' disappearing after 1.2 s with no next step nearby. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the first smaller issue, the tool grid scrolling sideways at 320 px. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the confirm page's 'Change' link returning to the basket without the current session ticked. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are 'Coming back to confirm also clears the details the member already typed'. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the three-tools-per-member rule not being enforced in the basket. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.

Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the hidden #c-tool copy making screen readers read the tool name twice (A titles it the done page, B the confirmation page; it is the same page). B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the 'Choose a pick-up session' error link pointing at a container that cannot take focus. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
Alignment by meaning; values agree. Both are the missing 'Skip to content' link on every page. B's number is one higher because of its R15/R16 split.
